title: Prostate & Male Urethra Anatomy: Zones, Ducts & Pathway
description: Master prostate and male urethra anatomy, detailing the peripheral, central, and transition zones, ejaculatory ducts, prostatic urethra, and nerve bundles.
h1: Prostate, Male Urethra and Ducts Anatomy: Zones and Relationships
blurb: McNeal's peripheral, central, and transition zones of the prostate surrounding the prostatic urethra where seminal vesicle and vas deferens ducts converge.
lead: Sitting immediately beneath the neck of the urinary bladder, the walnut-sized prostate surrounds the upper urethra at the exact junction where urinary and reproductive paths merge. In this illustrated guide to prostate gland and male urethra, we examine 21 documented structures—including bladder neck / internal sphincter, prostatic transition zone, prostatic peripheral zone, prostatic central zone—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Sitting immediately beneath the neck of the urinary bladder, the walnut-sized prostate surrounds the upper urethra at the exact junction where urinary and reproductive paths merge. A sagittal regional cut clarifies zones, bladder neck, ejaculatory duct entry and the urethral path through prostate and penis. Within the human body, the prostate, ducts & penis (Prostata et penis) is situated in bladder neck, pelvic floor and perineum, receives arterial perfusion via inferior vesical / internal pudendal branches, and is innervated by inferior hypogastric plexus + pudendal somatic branches.

Structurally, the bladder neck / internal sphincter (Collum vesicae) comprises smooth-muscle outlet superior to prostate. Physiologically, the bladder neck / internal sphincter closes during emission to limit retrograde ejaculation. Structurally, the prostatic transition zone (Zona transitionis) comprises zone surrounding proximal prostatic urethra. Physiologically, the prostatic transition zone contains glandular ducts and fibromuscular tissue. The prostatic peripheral zone (Zona peripherica) is posterior-lateral zone palpable through rectum. Physiologically, the prostatic peripheral zone produces prostatic secretions. Structurally, the prostatic central zone (Zona centralis) comprises tissue surrounding ejaculatory ducts. Physiologically, the prostatic central zone governs secretory prostatic gland region. Structurally, the prostatic urethra (Pars prostatica urethrae) comprises urethra through prostate from bladder neck to membrane. Physiologically, the prostatic urethra conducts urine and semen in separate phases. Structurally, the seminal colliculus (verumontanum) (Colliculus seminalis) comprises ridge in posterior prostatic urethra with duct openings. Physiologically, the seminal colliculus (verumontanum) governs landmark for ejaculatory duct openings.

Clinically, regarding the bladder neck / internal sphincter, bladder-neck dysfunction may affect voiding. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the prostatic transition zone, common origin of benign prostatic enlargement. In clinical pathology involving the prostatic peripheral zone, most prostatic cancers arise in this zone. Medical evaluation of the prostatic central zone also notes that less frequently a primary site of carcinoma.

questions.question: Where is the prostate located?
questions.answer: The prostate sits below the bladder and surrounds the first part of the urethra. Ducts from the reproductive tract open into the prostatic urethra. Structurally, the prostatic urethra (Pars prostatica urethrae) comprises urethra through prostate from bladder neck to membrane. Physiologically, the prostatic urethra conducts urine and semen in separate phases.

questions.question: What are the main anatomical zones of the prostate?
questions.answer: The transition, central and peripheral zones differ in location and surrounding structures. The peripheral zone occupies much of the posterior gland. Structurally, the anterior fibromuscular stroma comprises non-glandular anterior component of prostate rich in muscle and connective tissue. Physiologically, the anterior fibromuscular stroma provides structural support to prostatic urethra.

questions.question: What is the bladder neck / internal sphincter?
questions.answer: Smooth-muscle outlet superior to prostate. Functionally, it closes during emission to limit retrograde ejaculation. In clinical pathology involving the bladder neck / internal sphincter, bladder-neck dysfunction may affect voiding.

questions.question: Where is the prostatic peripheral zone located?
questions.answer: Posterior-lateral zone palpable through rectum. Functionally, it produces prostatic secretions. Medical evaluation of the prostatic peripheral zone also notes that most prostatic cancers arise in this zone.

questions.question: What is the function of the prostatic urethra?
questions.answer: Functionally, it conducts urine and semen in separate phases. Urethra through prostate from bladder neck to membrane. Structurally, the prostatic venous plexus comprises veins around capsule, communicating with deep dorsal penile and vesical veins. Physiologically, the prostatic venous plexus drain gland and adjacent bladder neck.
